[00:00:03] Anika: okay hey everyone thanks for joining on time i know it's a busy week so we'll run about 50 minutes and leave time for questions, quick housekeeping: slides and the recording will be posted.
[00:00:18] Diego: hi, quick add — we're going to fold a short tech update into the retrospective, just 8 minutes.
[00:00:25] Audience: applause (muted)
[00:00:30] Anika: great, so the Decision Lab ran for six weeks, many of you contributed experiments and we pulled together the top signals. Marcus, can you run through the three high level findings?
[00:00:42] Marcus: yeah thanks. Finding one: economics delta between hosted and dedicated is wider than we expected for rps-heavy workloads, mostly because of suboptimal batching defaults and some cold-start inefficiencies. finding two: observability — token-level cost attribution is incomplete for reranking and multi-model routes. finding three: onboarding friction — enterprise customers hit roadblocks on VPC/KMS and some of our contractual terms.
[00:01:10] Anika: thanks. are the batching defaults the main driver for the cost gap?
[00:01:14] Lena: that's part of it — default batch window was conservative to keep latency SLOs, but that left throughput on the table. plus our autoscaler thresholds are tuned for p99 latency, not median throughput, so we spin up GPUs too often.
[00:01:32] Diego: and to add — the runtime's kernel selection was picking more precise kernels for short sequences; we can tweak heuristics to prefer faster kernels when quantized models are deployed. there's a small risk to quality but the telemetry shows negligible regressions on our eval sets.
[00:01:52] [00:01:53] Speaker 1 (from audience): can you say a bit more about KV cache and prefix caching — i've seen customers lose a lot of tokens to repeated recompute?
[00:02:02] Lena: sure — KV cache is being under-utilized in multi-tenant pools because of eviction policies. during the lab we instrumented a few workloads and saw a 12-18% token reduction when prefix-level caching is preserved across similar sessions. note: some transcription earlier said K V cache like 'kay vee' which is funny.
[00:02:22] Marcus: the immediate play is to expose a 'session affinity' knob for Dedicated and tweak eviction to keep short-lived but high-reuse prefixes.
[00:02:30] [00:02:31] Priya: from go-to-market, customers are asking for clearer cost levers — they don't understand how batching, cache TTL, and quantization interact. Sales would like an operations playbook with examples (SaaS example, commerce example, and internal logs).
[00:02:48] Anika: excellent, that's a clear output. second big area was observability — Diego?
[00:02:54] Diego: yeah, token-level attribution currently splits evenly across model routes which is wrong for complex flows. we need per-route accounting in the console, and an ingestion pipeline change to carry session metadata into cost events. it's doable but needs backend and UI work.
[00:03:12] [00:03:13] Ethan: can i ask — how much of this is product vs infra? customers often just want a single number to show their finance team.
[00:03:20] Marcus: product will own the UX, infra will own the event schema and cost pipeline. we'll do a small spike during sprint 11.
[00:03:28] [00:03:29] Audience member (murmur): will this be in the console preview?
[00:03:34] Marcus: yes, minimal viable in console alpha then expand.
[00:03:36] Anika: the third area was onboarding friction, mostly enterprise concerns — VPC, KMS, SOC 2 and contractual language. Priya, status?
[00:03:45] Priya: legal and security have a working checklist. two blockers that came up: our template for data residency needs a clearer flow, and some customers push for an HSM/KMS integration that isn't just a doc change — that may require engineering work for key wrapping.
[00:03:59] [00:04:00] Diego: technical note: private plane control plane — sorry private control plane — is stable but the agent for customer-managed KMS needs additional testing. we had a flaky path in the on-prem package that the lab flagged.
[00:04:12] [00:04:13] Speaker 2 (voice): "socks two" was mentioned earlier in a sales call which hurt credibility — we need to fix how we talk about SOC 2.
[00:04:18] Anika: (laughs) yes, internal jargon cleanup. good catch.
[00:04:22] Anika: okay let's pivot — proposed roadmap reset: short window, three bets for Q2: (A) reliability and predictable economics (autoscaler + batching + cache); (B) enterprise pilot program for three anchor customers on Dedicated with prioritized legal/security support; (C) observability and cost-billing alpha in console.
[00:04:40] [00:04:41] Diego: technical milestones for A: autoscaler RFC this sprint, kernel-heuristic change in next two sprints, and a rollout to canary fleet by end of April.
[00:04:51] Lena: engineering followups: i will push the autoscaler tuning RFC by 2026-03-11. also we need to add load tests that mimic high-rps short-seq workloads.
[00:05:00] [00:05:01] Audience comment: "what about quantization recommendations? we saw model quality dips"
[00:05:06] Diego: we'll tie quantization profiles to eval suites and only suggest profiles that pass guardrails. Marcus will help prioritize which model families to cover.
[00:05:13] Marcus: yes, we have a short list.
[00:05:17] Anika: on B — enterprise pilot — Priya will lead, legal and security will be embedded, engineering will reserve a dedicated pool for pilot customers and offer hands-on onboarding. expected KPI: reduce time-to-first-query for pilot customers to under two business days.
[00:05:33] Priya: adding that sales will present pricing experiment options to pilot customers — fixed monthly plus overage vs committed throughput. we want to learn which sells better.
[00:05:44] [00:05:45] Audience: chatter about billing models
[00:05:47] Anika: on C — observability alpha — Marcus will own product, Diego infra, Ethan devrel will run enablement. timeline: alpha in mid-April, incremental releases through May.
[00:05:58] Ethan: enablement plan: docs, sample dashboards, and a workshop for top 20 customers.
[00:06:05] [00:06:06] Speaker 3 (interrupting): will we need extra headcount for this work?
[00:06:09] Anika: maybe temporarily — we will prioritize with hiring if needed. let's leave resourcing for the exec planning session.
[00:06:17] Anika: okay switching to open Q&A — please keep questions short so we can cover more.
[00:06:22] [00:06:23] Speaker 4: ops question — are we changing the SLA for Dedicated customers? I've seen threads asking for a stricter p99.
[00:06:31] Diego: no immediate SLA change; we'll propose a new SLA tier for enterprise pilot customers once autoscaler improvements and observability are validated. existing contracts remain unchanged.
[00:06:42] [00:06:43] Speaker 5: retention of audit logs — any changes?
[00:06:46] Lena: security is looking at configurable retention for audit logs behind an enterprise flag; likely an add-on. technical work is modest but legal signoff is required.
[00:06:56] Anika: great. quick shout on comms: we'll post a short blog/ops note explaining the Decision Lab outcomes and the Q2 bets; marketing will help craft messaging tailored to different customer segments.
[00:07:08] Priya: Marketing and Sales will sync tomorrow to align pilot outreach.
[00:07:12] [00:07:13] Anika: last 6 minutes — lightning updates from leaders. Diego?
[00:07:16] Diego: runtime improvements: shipped attention mem leak fix to canary, seeing 3-4% latency improvements. small rollback on one kernel change in staging; investigating.
[00:07:27] Lena: infra: new autoscaler metrics are in staging dashboards. need a few more synthetic runs.
[00:07:33] Marcus: product: Decision Lab reprioritization will be posted by end of week, with a clear list of must-haves vs nice-to-haves.
[00:07:40] Ethan: community: OSS sample app had 120 stars this week and a few PRs for improved docs. we'll highlight it in the ops note.
[00:07:48] Anika: ok wrap — recap of decisions: we reset Q2 around the three bets (reliability/economics, pilot program, observability alpha); owners and due dates in the action items. look for the condensed roadmap doc and the post with the Decision Lab summary.
[00:08:03] Anika: any final comments?
[00:08:05] [00:08:06] Speaker 6: thanks, good session.
[00:08:08] Anika: great, meeting adjourned.
